subject: empirical.tables and empirical.plot in itemfit() function

messages.author: 3be267a43e956fc4
messages.subject: empirical.tables and empirical.plot in itemfit() function
parts:
Hi, 
I'm trying to undestand how works the function itemfit(), specifically when I use this code: 

> data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
> model=mirt(data = data, model = 1, itemtype = "Rasch", SE=TRUE)
> itemfit(model, empirical.plot=1, empirical.CI=0.95)
> itemfit(model, empirical.table=1)

How do you get the Thetha value in empirical.table? are the same showed in empirical.plot option?  
how the intervals are constructed  in empirical.plot? 

Thanks a lot and i'm sorry about my very bad english.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: empirical.tables and empirical.plot in itemfit() function
parts:
The theta values are point estimates obtained via the fscores() function, which if not specified is executed according to the arguments in itemfit(). The intervals in the empirical plots correspond to large-sample confidence intervals based on the respective goodness-of-fit tests at each theta location implied by a beta distribution. Though note that these plots are approximations at best and only work well when the test length/sample size is sufficiently large to ensure the point estimates have reasonable measurement precision. HTH.

Phil
